changes: books/OT/genesis/Genesis_06.md
“Righteous.” One whose life aligns with covenantal faithfulness and justice.
“Righteous; just.” One characterized by right conduct or right standing.
books/OT/genesis/Genesis_29.md
“To kiss.” Gesture of recognition or covenantal greeting.
“To kiss.” A gesture of greeting, affection, or recognition.
books/OT/genesis/Genesis_01.md
“Spirit” or “wind.” Denotes divine presence and movement.
“Spirit; wind; breath.” The term has a broad semantic range; context determines the sense.
books/OT/exodus/Exodus_37.md
“Cherubim.” Winged heavenly beings associated with divine presence.
“Cherubim.” Winged heavenly beings associated with the ark and divine throne imagery.
books/OT/exodus/Exodus_03.md
“Fire.” Manifestation of divine presence.
“Fire.” Here the fire appears within the bush in the divine encounter.
books/OT/exodus/Exodus_03.md
“Holiness.” Set-apartness defined by God’s presence.
“Holiness; holy place.” That which is set apart or sacred.
books/OT/1chronicles/1Chronicles_02.md
This term means "firstborn," often indicating a privileged status in familial inheritance and responsibility within biblical narratives.
“Firstborn.” The term can mark birth order and the status attached to the firstborn within a household.
books/OT/jonah/Jonah_02.md
“Your holy temple.” The place associated with God's presence and worship.
“Your holy temple.” The sanctuary toward which the prayer is directed.
books/OT/1kings/1Kings_19.md
The name of the deity whose worship has shaped the conflict of the preceding chapter. Kneeling and kissing are named as acts of allegiance that the faithful remnant has refused.
“Baal.” The name of the deity whose worship dominates the preceding conflict.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_07.md
“Meaning "vision," this refers to revelation typically received by prophets.”
“Vision.” A prophetic vision or revelatory sight.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_15.md
“The word of Yahweh" — A common biblical phrase indicating the communication of Yahweh's will through a prophet.
“Word of the LORD.” A standard prophetic formula introducing a received message.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_47.md
— “to heal.” The waters are healed, and the verb frames the river’s effect as restoration from death-bearing salinity to life.
“To heal.” The verb describes the waters becoming restored from death-bearing salinity to life.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_22.md
“The word" of the LORD introduces the divine message to Ezekiel.
“Word; matter.” Here the term introduces the message spoken to Ezekiel.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_16.md
to prostitute oneself.: Repeated throughout the chapter, this verb gives the controlling metaphor for Jerusalem’s covenantal betrayal through idolatry and foreign alliances.
“To prostitute oneself.” The repeated verb supplies the chapter’s controlling metaphor for Jerusalem’s unfaithfulness.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_16.md
iniquity, guilt.: Sodom’s avon is specified in social as well as cultic terms: pride, abundance, ease, and neglect of the poor and needy.
“Iniquity; guilt.” The term here introduces the wrong attributed to Sodom.
books/OT/ezekiel/Ezekiel_16.md
everlasting, enduring.: In “everlasting covenant,” the word gives the final promise a horizon beyond the immediate judgment.
“Everlasting; enduring.” In “everlasting covenant,” the term extends the promise beyond the immediate judgment.
books/OT/zephaniah/Zephaniah_02.md
The repeated imperative presses the shameless nation to collect or gather itself before judgment comes.
“To gather; collect.” The repeated imperative creates an insistent summons.
books/OT/zephaniah/Zephaniah_03.md
The term describes the city as oppressive or violent. Its use frames the chapter’s condemnation around the city’s abuse of power.
“Oppressing; violent.” The adjective characterizes the city’s conduct.
books/OT/psalms/Psalm_135.md
“Here, have compassion or relent, describing God’s responsive mercy toward the servants.”
“To relent; have compassion.” The verb can describe a change in announced action or a movement of compassion.
books/OT/psalms/Psalm_058.md
Here translated as “silent,” suggesting inactivity or failure to act, in contrast with the expectation of just verdicts from those expected to judge righteously.
“Silent.” The difficult Hebrew form may describe silence or failure to render judgment.
books/OT/psalms/Psalm_088.md
The realm of the dead; retained because English equivalents such as “grave” or “hell” are narrower than the Hebrew term.
“Sheol; realm of the dead.” The Hebrew term is broader than English “grave” and does not by itself carry the later associations of “hell.”
books/OT/psalms/Psalm_062.md
This enduring love or covenant loyalty underpins divine justice as it connects with divine recompense for human actions.
“Steadfast love; covenant loyalty.” Reliable love expressed in faithful action.
books/NT/matthew/Matthew_17.md
“Cloud; a traditional marker of divine presence and concealment.”
“Cloud.” In biblical theophanic scenes, a cloud can mark presence and concealment.
books/NT/mark/Mark_12.md
“Vineyard.” A cultivated field, often carrying covenantal resonance.
“Vineyard.” A cultivated field of grapevines; the image carries established scriptural associations.
books/NT/romans/Romans_12.md
“Sacrifice.” Traditionally a ritual offering, here reconfigured as lived devotion.
“Sacrifice; offering.” Here the ritual term is applied metaphorically to embodied life.
books/NT/acts/Acts_07.md
“Glory.” Denotes divine presence and radiance; often associated with revelation.
“Glory.” Honor, splendor, or manifest radiance; here in the title “God of glory.”
